title: Extract `_run_quality_gate` helper from `_run_ralph_loop_node` on `RalphWorkflowEngine`
summary: Behavior-preserving refactor inside `src/kodezart/chains/ralph_workflow.py`: lift the `async for event in self._quality_gate.run(...)` block (currently inlined in `_run_ralph_loop_node` lines 462–481) into a new private async helper `RalphWorkflowEngine._run_quality_gate(...)` on the same class, then collapse the caller body to delegate. The helper is a transparent forwarder of the `QualityGate.run` protocol contract — its kwargs are the protocol's kwargs, verbatim — and returns the final `WorkflowIterationEvent` directly. Zero runtime semantics change. Zero graph-shape change. Zero protocol change. Zero state-shape change. Zero new imports. Exactly one caller post-change; a second caller is explicitly out of scope.
context:
**Why this change.** A follow-up change will introduce a second caller for the same `self._quality_gate.run(...)` invocation pattern. The minimum-blast-radius preparatory step is to extract the inline loop into a private helper now, as a pure refactor with no behavior change, so the follow-up reduces to a single `await self._run_quality_gate(...)` invocation.

**Revision history (corrects four reviewer-flagged defects in the prior draft):**
- *Defect 1 — Ruff ANN401 false positive on `StreamWriter` alias.* The Ruff documentation for ANN401 ([docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/any-type/](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/any-type/)) explicitly notes: "Type aliases are unsupported and can lead to false positives. For example, the following will trigger this rule inadvertently: `MyAny = Any`." Since `langgraph.types.StreamWriter = Callable[[Any], None]` (verified at `.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/langgraph/types.py:111`), annotating `writer: StreamWriter` would fire ANN401 under the repo's active `ANN` rule set in `pyproject.toml`. Anti-pattern 9 forbids `# noqa`, so `make lint` would fail. **Resolution:** drop the `StreamWriter` import entirely; do NOT take a `writer` parameter.
- *Defect 2 — `(WorkflowIterationEvent, int)` tuple return duplicates information.* The `int` was `last_iteration_event.iteration` — readable from the event itself by a zero-cost attribute access. YAGNI. **Resolution:** return `WorkflowIterationEvent` directly; caller reads `.accepted` and `.iteration` from it.
- *Defect 3 — 6-kwarg ad-hoc signature invents a third contract.* The prior draft's 6 kwargs were neither the 10-kwarg `QualityGate.run` protocol contract at `src/kodezart/core/protocols.py:416–434` nor the existing typed domain model `RalphLoopContext` at `src/kodezart/types/domain/workflow.py:59–64` (which `ralph_loop.py:84–95` already uses as the canonical aggregation of loop-specific fields). The reviewer offered both shapes — protocol-passthrough OR `RalphLoopContext`. **Resolution:** option (a) — protocol-passthrough — chosen because `RalphLoopContext.acceptance_criteria: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)` would introduce a Pydantic validation step at the helper boundary that does NOT exist pre-refactor (the original code passes `state["acceptance_criteria"]` straight to the protocol without intermediate validation). Option (b) would violate the strict "ZERO runtime semantics change" mandate by adding a new pre-call validation failure mode. Option (a) is a transparent forwarder of the protocol — single contract, zero validation drift.
- *Defect 4 — wrong rationale for taking `writer` as a parameter.* The "contextvar propagation" justification is incorrect on Python 3.12. The LangGraph reference for `get_stream_writer` ([reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph/config/get_stream_writer](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph/config/get_stream_writer)) and the streaming guide ([docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/streaming](https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/streaming)) state that `get_stream_writer()` requires Python ≥ 3.11 for contextvar propagation in async code; this project's `pyproject.toml:6` declares `requires-python = ">=3.12"`, so contextvar propagation is guaranteed. Calls from `await`-edges inside the node body inherit the contextvar context. The other eight `writer = get_stream_writer()` sites in this same file (lines 370, 399, 455, 544, 647, 742, 848, 937, 1037 — established by Explore Agent 1 in prior research) all rely on this inline idiom. **Resolution:** the helper calls `get_stream_writer()` inline, matching the file's local convention.

Additional reviewer suggestions applied:
- Renamed `_run_loop_for` → `_run_quality_gate` (verb-noun, matches `_resolve_cwd` convention in this file; `_run_loop_for` has no precedent suffix).
- Docstring shortened to a single semantic line, matching the caller's `"""Delegate to the quality gate for iterative execution."""`.
- Corrected reference: `from_configurable` is defined on `WorkflowContext` at `src/kodezart/types/domain/workflow.py:38–48` and inherited by `ExecutionContext` (subclass at lines 51–56). The previous draft's "at 38-48 (inherited via the subclass at line 51)" was technically right but misleadingly worded; this revision attaches the line range to the parent class explicitly.

requiredChanges.description:
Two edits, both inside `class RalphWorkflowEngine`, both behavior-preserving. **Zero new imports.** Zero changes outside this class.

**Edit 1 (sub-step a) — ADD `_run_quality_gate` as a private async instance method on `RalphWorkflowEngine`, immediately ABOVE `_run_ralph_loop_node`** (i.e. inserted before the current line 448 so a top-to-bottom reader meets the helper before its caller). Exact signature and body:

```python
async def _run_quality_gate(
    self,
    *,
    prompt: str,
    repo_path: str | None,
    repo_url: str | None,
    feature_branch: str,
    ralph_branch: str,
    base_branch: str,
    permission_mode: str,
    allowed_tools: list[str],
    acceptance_criteria: list[str],
    cache_key: str,
) -> WorkflowIterationEvent:
    """Delegate to the quality gate for iterative execution."""
    writer = get_stream_writer()
    last_iteration_event: WorkflowIterationEvent | None = None
    async for event in self._quality_gate.run(
        prompt=prompt,
        repo_path=repo_path,
        repo_url=repo_url,
        feature_branch=feature_branch,
        ralph_branch=ralph_branch,
        base_branch=base_branch,
        permission_mode=permission_mode,
        allowed_tools=allowed_tools,
        acceptance_criteria=acceptance_criteria,
        cache_key=cache_key,
    ):
        writer(event)
        if isinstance(event, WorkflowIterationEvent):
            last_iteration_event = event

    if last_iteration_event is None:
        msg = "Ralph loop completed without emitting an iteration event."
        raise RuntimeError(msg)

    return last_iteration_event
```

**Signature constraints (each load-bearing):**
- Keyword-only after `self` (the `*` separator). Mirrors the `QualityGate.run` protocol contract at `src/kodezart/core/protocols.py:416–434` byte-for-byte (same 10 kwargs, same order, same types). The helper is a transparent forwarder — it introduces NO new contract.
- Return type is `WorkflowIterationEvent` (NOT a tuple). The caller reads `.accepted` and `.iteration` from the returned event — both are zero-cost attribute accesses already present on the event.
- NO `writer` parameter. `get_stream_writer()` is called inline, matching the 8 other writer call sites in this same file. Python ≥ 3.12 (per `pyproject.toml:6`) guarantees contextvar propagation across the `await` boundary, so the writer obtained inside the helper is the SAME writer the calling node would have obtained — the SSE stream is connected.
- NO `StreamWriter` import. The previous draft's `from langgraph.types import StreamWriter` was removed because (i) annotating `writer: StreamWriter` trips Ruff ANN401 as a documented type-alias false positive, (ii) Anti-pattern 9 forbids `# noqa`, and (iii) the parameter itself is removed (see prior point).
- Single-line docstring matches the caller's existing docstring style.

**Body constraints (each load-bearing):**
- The 10 kwargs forwarded to `self._quality_gate.run(...)` are positionally and semantically identical to the original (lines 463–474 of the pre-refactor file), modulo source: they now arrive as direct kwargs to the helper rather than as `state["..."]` / `ctx....` reads inside the same function.
- `writer(event)` is byte-identical.
- `if isinstance(event, WorkflowIterationEvent): last_iteration_event = event` is byte-identical.
- The terminal `if last_iteration_event is None: raise RuntimeError(...)` block is byte-identical. The error string MUST remain exactly `"Ralph loop completed without emitting an iteration event."` — do not reword.
- Zero `state` mutation. The helper has no access to `state`.
- Zero return-dict construction. The helper returns the event; the caller builds the LangGraph state-merge dict.

**Edit 2 (sub-step b) — REFACTOR `_run_ralph_loop_node` to delegate.** Replace lines 455 (the `writer = get_stream_writer()` line moves INTO the helper, so this line is DELETED from the caller) and lines 462–489 (lift target). Lines 448–454 (signature, docstring, `ctx = ExecutionContext.from_configurable(config)`) and lines 457–460(the `state["ticket"] is None` precondition + error string) are byte-identical.

```python
async def _run_ralph_loop_node(
    self,
    state: WorkflowState,
    config: RunnableConfig,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Delegate to the quality gate for iterative execution."""
    ctx = ExecutionContext.from_configurable(config)

    ticket = state["ticket"]
    if ticket is None:
        msg = "run_ralph_loop requires a ticket but state['ticket'] is None."
        raise RuntimeError(msg)

    last_iteration_event = await self._run_quality_gate(
        prompt=format_ticket_as_task(ticket),
        repo_path=ctx.repo_path,
        repo_url=ctx.repo_url,
        feature_branch=state["feature_branch"],
        ralph_branch=state["ralph_branch"],
        base_branch=ctx.base_branch,
        permission_mode=ctx.permission_mode,
        allowed_tools=ctx.allowed_tools,
        acceptance_criteria=state["acceptance_criteria"],
        cache_key=ctx.cache_key,
    )

    # feature_tip_sha is left None here; _merge_to_feature_node sets it
    # from the merger's outcome.feature_tip_sha (canonical, post-push).
    return {
        "accepted": last_iteration_event.accepted,
        "total_iterations": last_iteration_event.iteration,
        "feature_tip_sha": None,
    }
```

**Caller constraints (each load-bearing):**
- `ctx = ExecutionContext.from_configurable(config)` STAYS — it is LangGraph-context-bound (reads `config["configurable"]`), so it must run inside the node body.
- `writer = get_stream_writer()` is REMOVED from the caller. It now lives inside the helper. The 9-line helper body still produces an identical SSE stream because contextvar propagation across `await` makes the writer obtained inside the helper functionally identical to the writer the caller would have obtained.
- The `state["ticket"] is None` precondition STAYS in the caller. Error string byte-identical: `"run_ralph_loop requires a ticket but state['ticket'] is None."`.
- The return dict's three keys (`accepted`, `total_iterations`, `feature_tip_sha`) and value semantics are byte-identical. `total_iterations = last_iteration_event.iteration` (was `last_iteration_event.iteration` pre-refactor; same expression, just spelled against the returned event).
- The two-line comment `# feature_tip_sha is left None here; _merge_to_feature_node sets it / # from the merger's outcome.feature_tip_sha (canonical, post-push).` stays verbatim.
- The docstring `"""Delegate to the quality gate for iterative execution."""` stays verbatim.

**Sub-step (c) — single-caller invariant.** Do NOT add any second invocation of `_run_quality_gate` in `src/`. After this change, `git grep -n "_run_quality_gate" src/kodezart/chains/ralph_workflow.py` returns exactly 2 hits: the `async def _run_quality_gate` definition line, and the `await self._run_quality_gate(` call inside `_run_ralph_loop_node`.

**No-new-imports invariant.** All names used in the new helper (`WorkflowIterationEvent`, `get_stream_writer`) are already imported in the file at lines 53 and 8 respectively. Confirm `git diff src/kodezart/chains/ralph_workflow.py | grep -E "^\+from |^\+import "` returns zero lines.
requiredChanges.rationale:
**Defect-1 fix (lint compliance):** dropping the `StreamWriter` parameter eliminates the ANN401 false positive documented at [docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/any-type/](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/rules/any-type/) (“Type aliases are unsupported and can lead to false positives… `MyAny = Any`”), so `make lint` stays green without any suppression directive.

**Defect-2 fix (YAGNI):** returning `WorkflowIterationEvent` directly removes the duplicate `int` field; the caller reads `.iteration` and `.accepted` from the single returned value.

**Defect-3 fix (contract discipline):** the 10-kwarg keyword-only signature mirrors the `QualityGate.run` protocol exactly. The helper IS the protocol contract — no third ad-hoc contract is invented, and no Pydantic validation step is introduced (which would have happened if the helper accepted a `RalphLoopContext` whose `acceptance_criteria: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)` validator could fire). The strict “ZERO runtime semantics change” mandate is preserved.

**Defect-4 fix (correct local convention):** moving `get_stream_writer()` into the helper matches the 8 other inline call sites in this file. On Python ≥ 3.12 (the project floor at `pyproject.toml:6`), the [LangGraph docs](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph/config/get_stream_writer) confirm contextvar propagation works across awaited callees — the writer obtained inside `_run_quality_gate` is the SAME writer the calling node would have obtained.

**Naming:** `_run_quality_gate` follows the verb-noun convention seen in `_resolve_cwd` elsewhere in this file; the previous `_run_loop_for` had no precedent suffix.

**Behavior preservation:** the lifted loop body is byte-equivalent to the original lines 462–481. Existing integration tests at `tests/chains/test_ralph_workflow.py:1080–1147` and `:2396–2499` continue to assert the same SSE event sequences end-to-end via `engine.run(...)` — the helper is exercised transitively, no test edit needed.
